questions.q: What is the actual difference between a struct and a class in C++?
options: A struct cannot have member functions
A class cannot be copied
Members default to public in a struct and private in a class
A struct can only contain built-in types
questions.explain: struct and class are the same language feature; the only difference is the default access level of their members.

questions.q: In the Position class example, why is addFill() the only function allowed to modify qty_ and avgPrice_?
options: Because private members can only be changed by one function
Because it ensures both values are recomputed together, so they can never drift out of sync
Because C++ requires exactly one setter per class
It isn't — any public function could modify them
questions.explain: Encapsulation routes every change through a single method that updates both related members together, preserving the class's invariant.

questions.q: Why must a const data member be set in the member-initializer list rather than the constructor body?
options: The initializer list runs faster on all compilers
A const member cannot be assigned to at all after it is initialized, and the constructor body only runs after initialization
C++ forbids const members from having any value
It is only a style convention, not a requirement
questions.explain: By the time the constructor body executes, all members are already initialized; a const member can never be assigned afterward, so it must receive its value in the initializer list.

questions.q: What does marking a member function const (e.g. double quantity() const) tell the compiler?
options: The function returns a compile-time constant
The function cannot be called at all
The function promises not to modify the object's state, so it can be called on a const object or reference
The function's return value cannot be stored in a variable
questions.explain: A const member function guarantees it won't modify the object, which is what allows it to be invoked through a const reference.

questions.q: If you declare no constructor at all for a class, what happens?
options: The code fails to compile
The compiler generates a default constructor for you
All members are automatically initialized to zero regardless of type
The class becomes a struct automatically
questions.explain: When no constructor is declared, the compiler generates a default one (though it may do little or nothing for members without their own default initialization).
